diagnosis: The gate failed because rollout 1 failed content check C6, which gates fact PF2 (owner A3). In rollout 1, PF2 was properly revealed by A3 at turn 2 and correctly cited in justification_fact_ids, so this is not a disclosure or telepathy problem. The failure is an ENCODING MISMATCH: C6 requires a commitment referencing 'generator-backed power' in connection with the clinic, pharmacy, vaccine refrigerator, or primary feed transfer. The clinic commitment in rollout 1 reads 'Ensure the pharmacy technician's vaccine refrigerator power note is added to the base power plan' — it mentions 'vaccine refrigerator' but drops the phrase 'generator-backed power,' substituting the vaguer 'power note.' The three passing rollouts (0, 2, 3) all explicitly include 'generator-backed power' in their clinic commitments, which is why C6 passed for them. All other checks (C1–C5, C7–C8, P1–P3) passed in all four rollouts, and no rollout hit the turn cap.

C6.why: The vaccine refrigerator requirement changes the clinic transfer window to exactly 1000-1200 and requires a commitment referencing generator-backed power in connection with the clinic, pharmacy, vaccine refrigerator, or primary feed transfer.

fix_instructions: Broaden the wording threshold of check C6 so it does not strictly require the exact phrase 'generator-backed power.' Currently C6 demands both 'generator-backed power' AND one of (clinic, pharmacy, vaccine refrigerator, primary feed transfer) in the commitment text. In rollout 1 the model encoded the same information as 'vaccine refrigerator power note,' which a human would accept but the check rejects. Revise C6 to accept any commitment that references 'generator' or 'generator-backed' OR 'vaccine refrigerator' in combination with a power-transfer concept, or alternatively accept 'primary feed transfer' alone. This ENCODING MISMATCH on C6 (gating PF2) is the sole failure mode driving the gate failure; no changes to shared_context, agent personalities, or disclosure norms are needed since PF2 was revealed and cited correctly in every rollout.
